title: Port Build 7 ECR -2 to Build 8: Flrt3: Horn state doesn't change on brake/horn interface screen
executive_summary: This change fixes a horn state display bug specific to SR-FLRT3-DMU units on the brake/horn interface screen—when the horn key is pressed, the state field should update to Active but currently stays showing Inactive. The fix is well-targeted with seven high-priority tests (L2R05:TC1, L2R01:TC1, L2R05:TC3, L2R05:TC4, L2R01:TC2, L2R05:TC2, L2R01:TC3) that directly cover the two core requirements L2R01 and L2R05. However, you need to watch for regressions in related brake and depart test logic, as past defects in these areas were high-severity and have reoccurred before. Four affected requirements lack test evidence (L2R1644, L2R508, L2R615, L2R1234), creating coverage gaps despite passing evidence in EV-4001 and EV-4011.

ecr_overview.title: Port Build 7 ECR -2 to Build 8: Flrt3: Horn state doesn't change on brake/horn interface screen
ecr_overview.description:
When the Horn key is pressed on the "brake/horn interface" screen, Ob doesn't update the Horn state field to Active, and it continues to show Inactive on the screen.

This is working fine on "EBI Slot 6 - EBI Onboard Diagnostics" and "System Test - Brakes" Screen.

This issue is only observed for SR-FLRT3-DMU. For SR-KSS_EMU, Ob is working correctly.

change_classification.summary: The horn state display on the brake/horn interface screen is not updating to Active when the horn key is pressed on FLRT3 units, even though it works correctly on other screens and vehicle types. The fix modifies how the interface screen renders horn state and how diagnostics processes horn state updates.

sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.body: This change fixes a horn state display bug specific to SR-FLRT3-DMU units on the brake/horn interface screen—when the horn key is pressed, the state field should update to Active but currently stays showing Inactive. The fix is well-targeted with seven high-priority tests (L2R05:TC1, L2R01:TC1, L2R05:TC3, L2R05:TC4, L2R01:TC2, L2R05:TC2, L2R01:TC3) that directly cover the two core requirements L2R01 and L2R05. However, you need to watch for regressions in related brake and depart test logic, as past defects in these areas were high-severity and have reoccurred before. Four affected requirements lack test evidence (L2R1644, L2R508, L2R615, L2R1234), creating coverage gaps despite passing evidence in EV-4001 and EV-4011.
